title: Model Metadata Schema + Automated Release Notes — PRD Outline (WIP)
content:
Doc owner: Paula
Last working session: 2025-10-11 (notes merged from Marissa + Dylan + Connor)

Context / why this doc exists
- We keep getting the same customer question in escalations: “Did my model change? What changed? How risky is it? How do I roll back?”
- Internally model/version info is fragmented:
  - model registry has some fields (name, family, a few config bits)
  - runtime configs live elsewhere (batching/kv-cache/quant profile)
  - release notes are manual + inconsistent + sometimes missing
- With Unified Rollouts + A/B testing, the change surface is bigger: promotions, canaries, policy-based routing, fallback models.
- Goal is a single metadata schema v1 as source-of-truth + an automated customer-visible changelog/release notes generator.

Working PRD outline (WIP)

1) Problem statement
- Today we cannot reliably answer:
  - what changed between model version A and B
  - where/when it changed (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
  - who approved it + what evidence exists (eval runs, quality checks)
  - whether a customer was impacted (rollout policy + timing)
- Outcomes:
  - Silent changes → output drift tickets (ex: SUP-28429)
  - Missing release notes for promotions (ex: SUP-28411)
  - Enterprise procurement blockers for regulated customers (Northbridge)

2) Customer & internal user personas (who we build for)
- Customer: ML/platform engineer pinning versions + needs predictable change control.
- Customer: app engineer using latest (un-pinned) + needs “what changed” context when behavior shifts.
- Support / CS: needs to answer “what changed for this account” quickly without engineering.
- Release engineering: wants required checks, preview artifacts, consistent taxonomy.
- Docs team: wants a feed/artifact they can publish with minimal manual editing.
- Security/compliance: wants audit event coverage + retention/export story.

3) Goals (draft)
- Define and adopt model metadata schema v1 across served models/variants/quant profiles.
- Generate customer-visible release notes automatically from metadata changes + promotion events.
- Provide internal auditability: who changed what + when + tie to rollout/promotion.
- Improve rollout safety and customer trust (less “surprise drift”).

Non-goals (for MVP)
- Full notification subscriptions (email/webhook) to customers (we may add basic internal webhook plumbing only).
- Perfect historical backfill: aim for forward-looking generation; limited backfill for top models only.
- Replacing the eval system; we only reference eval evidence via IDs / summaries.

4) Early customer feedback (summarized)
Northbridge Capital Markets (Private / regulated)
- Procurement blocker: they need an auditable record of model changes (who/when/what) and retention controls.
- Explicit ask: customer-visible release notes per upgrade bundle, including deprecation timelines.
- They want to ensure we do NOT leak internal incident info or internal safety findings.

Lattice Health Systems (Dedicated)
- Wants per-model change history in Console.
- Wants to understand what “A/B test” means when their traffic is split (i.e., which model variants were involved).
- Needs rollback guidance when metrics regress.

Support tickets
- SUP-28429: “output regression after silent model change” → support couldn’t quickly map request timestamps to rollout event + model promotion.
- SUP-28411: “release notes missing” → enterprise expectation mismatch; even when change is “minor,” they require a note.

5) User stories (rough)
Customer
- As a customer, I can view release notes for a model version I’m using (or was routed to) and understand:
  - category (breaking/perf/quality/bugfix/security/deprecation)
  - affected deployments (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
  - compatibility notes (tokenizer/runtime constraints)
  - rollout guidance / rollback guidance
- As a customer, I can see a per-model change history feed and filter by deployment/region.

Support / CS
- As support, I can see internal-only details (e.g., internal incident references, eval run IDs) and correlate account impact.
- As support, I can export a concise changelog snippet for a customer escalation.

Release Eng
- As release eng, metadata changes are validated in CI with a release-note preview artifact.
- As release eng, “promotion to default” triggers a release note entry automatically.

Docs
- As docs, I can publish a public release notes page/feed with minimal editing; embargo/customer-specific notes are supported.

6) Product requirements (draft / MVP)
6.1 Metadata schema v1 (what must exist)
- Model identity fields
  - model_id (stable), display_name, model_family
  - variant identifiers (instruction/chat, context length, tool calling support)
  - quantization profile (if applicable)
- Versioning
  - semantic version for serving behavior (see open question: what exactly semver means here)
  - support for “build metadata” / internal revision id
  - compatibility constraints (tokenizer version, runtime engine minimum, function calling schema versions, etc.)
- Deployment availability
  - hosted: true/false + regions
  - dedicated: true/false + constraints
  - private: true/false + supported bundle versions
- Public vs internal fields
  - clear strategy to avoid leaking sensitive/internal-only details
  - required redaction/field filtering rules for customer-visible output
- Deprecation lifecycle
  - deprecated_at, deprecation_reason (public), deprecation_timeline
  - replacement model/version suggestions
- Rollout eligibility
  - whether version can be used in canary/A-B
  - policy constraints (e.g., “not eligible for regulated workloads until guardrails pass”)
- Safety/quality notes (careful wording)
  - optional: “known limitations” + “quality notes”
  - optional: guardrail outcomes summary (no raw internal metrics in public field by default)

6.2 Changelog/release notes generation
- Inputs
  - metadata change events (create/update)
  - version promotion events (e.g., set as default)
  - optional: PR label/annotation to improve the human narrative (hybrid approach?)
- Output
  - customer-visible release notes entry with taxonomy + consistent phrasing
  - internal entry includes extra context (approver, links, eval IDs)
  - stable IDs for entries for linking from Console + docs
- Templates and language guidelines
  - categories: security, breaking, performance, quality, bugfix, deprecation
  - severity levels: (TBD) maybe “low/medium/high” or “informational/attention/action required”
  - avoid claiming statistical improvements unless evidence threshold met

6.3 Console surfaces (MVP)
- Per-model “Change history” tab
  - chronological list with filters: deployment mode, region, timeframe
  - entries show effective date(s) for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private where available
- Release notes feed
  - global feed + model-scoped feed
  - show “you are pinned to X” and “latest is Y”
- Access control / RBAC
  - internal-only fields must never render to customer roles
  - support role: can see internal notes (audit view)

6.4 Docs publishing (MVP)
- Public release notes pages by model + global feed
- URLs stable and versioned
- Handling embargoed notes (Private/customer-specific) without leaking publicly

6.5 Audit logging (MVP)
- Emit structured audit events for:
  - metadata created/updated
  - version promoted/demoted
  - deprecation set/changed
- Retention + export (at minimum: internal retention; SIEM export TBD)

7) MVP scope proposal (rough cut)
Must-have for MVP
- Metadata schema v1 + validation tooling in CI (block merges)
- Migration/backfill for existing model records (only required fields)
- Event emission from control plane / registry updates
- Generator produces:
  - customer-safe release note entry (public)
  - internal entry with richer context
- Console:
  - minimal change history view (list + filters)
  - release notes view per model
- Docs:
  - publish generated public notes for a subset of models (top 10 by usage)
- Redaction rules + tests (ensure no internal field leaks)

Nice-to-have (post-MVP)
- Customer notification subscriptions
- Per-account “impact view” (which account saw which version when)
- Richer quality summaries with significance + confidence
- Full historical backfill

8) Open questions (please resolve)
Schema semantics
- What exactly does semantic versioning mean for a model?
  - If weights change but “expected behavior” is mostly same, is that minor or patch?
  - If tokenizer changes, is that always major/breaking?
- Do we need separate versions for:
  - weights
  - serving runtime / kernels
  - quant profile
  - safety/guardrails config
  (Or do we represent all in one “served artifact version”?)

Source of truth & workflow
- Where is the authoritative record edited? (model registry vs control plane vs Git repo)
- Who can edit public release note text vs auto-generated text?
- Approval workflow for public notes: PM? Release Eng? Security for certain categories?

Public vs internal
- Field-level access model:
  - explicit public fields + explicit internal fields
  - or “everything public unless marked internal”? (seems dangerous)
- Do we allow “customer-specific internal notes” separate from general internal? (e.g., for a Private customer bundle)

Changelog generation inputs
- Event-only vs GitHub PR labels vs hybrid
  - If event-only: how do we get narrative/context beyond field diffs?
  - If PR-label: how do we guarantee coverage for non-code changes (e.g., registry edits)?
- Do we require a “release note summary” field on promotions?

Rollouts / A-B testing
- During an A/B, what do we show to the customer?
  - Do we show both versions and the period they were active?
  - How do we message “experimental/limited rollout” without causing panic?

Private deployments
- How do upgrade bundles map to model promotions?
  - Is the release note keyed by model version or bundle version or both?
- Offline environments: how do we deliver release note artifacts with the bundle?

Quality signals
- Which metrics can be publicly referenced, and at what threshold?
- What is the minimum evidence we require to say “improved quality”?
- Who signs off on quality language?

9) Success metrics (draft)
- Coverage
  - % of model promotions with generated release notes (target: 95%+)
- Support impact
  - reduce tickets tagged “silent model change” (baseline from SUP tickets)
  - time-to-answer for “what changed?” in escalations
- Product adoption
  - Console engagement: views of change history/release notes for top customers
- Quality/regression detection
  - correlation: fewer “unknown change” incidents; faster rollback when regressions happen

10) Dependencies / stakeholders (notes)
Stakeholders
- Product: Marissa (lead), Paula (rollout policy), Elliot/Wei (Docs)
- Eng: Dylan (lead), Chloe (Console backend), Ethan (control plane), Quentin (schema), Connor (release)
- Security/compliance: Naomi + Marcus
- Support/CS: Dev + Miguel

Known dependencies
- Model registry schema work + migrations (ENG-9821 / ENG-9822)
- Eventing (control plane) (ENG-9823)
- Console endpoints + UI (ENG-9824)
- Redaction rules + security review (ENG-9825)
- CI preview artifact + gating (ENG-9826)
- Evals tags / evidence linking (ENG-9827)
- Audit events (ENG-9828)
- Private bundle export (ENG-9829)

11) Risks / edge cases (quick list)
- Leaking internal-only notes publicly (we already had a near-miss / UI bug class here; needs strong tests + default deny)
- Overstating quality improvements without stat sig
- Customers pinned to versions: must preserve old metadata and old release notes permanently
- Multi-deployment drift: Hosted gets updates faster than Dedicated/Private → confusing timelines
- Backfill gaps: some existing models may not have required fields (esp tokenizer/runtime constraints)

12) MVP rollout plan (sketch)
- Phase 0: schema draft + examples + validation in CI (non-blocking initially)
- Phase 1: migrations/backfill + event emission
- Phase 2: generator + Console internal dogfood (support/admin view first)
- Phase 3: public docs pages for subset of models + enterprise beta (Northbridge/Lattice candidates via PM-413)
- Phase 4: GA + required checks enforced (CI becomes blocking)

Notes to self / TODO
- Pull in concrete examples of “breaking change” vs “non-breaking” from Connor + Docs style guide work (need canonical examples for reviewers)
- Schedule 30 min with Security to align on audit retention + SIEM export expectations
- Decide on the semver policy proposal and get sign-off (Marissa + Quentin + Dylan)
- Confirm MVP “top models by usage” list with Model Catalog (Quentin)
